fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. Jesus cries out, “Whoever believes in Me does not believe in Me alone, but in the One who sent Me.” (John 12:44) Believing in Jesus reaches the One who sent Him too. Jesus names no one else here, so the answer is the One who sent Him.

Right, friend. Jesus says, “And whoever sees Me sees the One who sent Me.” (John 12:45) Just before this, He said that believing in Him means believing in the One who sent Him (John 12:44). The two lines go together: whether someone believes in Jesus or sees Jesus, it reaches the One who sent Him.

That's a fair guess, but it's not the word Jesus uses. He says, “For I have not come to judge the world, but to save the world.” (John 12:47) He is saying why He came, and He puts judging on one side and saving on the other. Testing isn't on either side, so the blank is save.

Rule makes sense as a guess, but Jesus doesn't use it. He says, “For I have not come to judge the world, but to save the world.” (John 12:47) He puts judging next to saving, which tells us the reason He came is to save. Ruling isn't part of that sentence, so the blank is save.
